questions.explanation: Hash tables use a hash function to map keys to indices, allowing for average O(1) operations. However, collisions can lead to O(n) worst-case performance.
questions.question: Which data structure provides average O(1) time complexity for insertion, deletion, and retrieval, but can degrade to O(n) in the worst case?

questions.correct_answer: Efficient searching with an average time complexity of O(log n)
questions.explanation: Binary Search Trees allow for efficient searching, insertion, and deletion with an average time complexity of O(log n). The worst-case scenario for a BST can be O(n) if the tree becomes unbalanced.
options: Guaranteed O(log n) search time in all cases
Efficient searching with an average time complexity of O(log n)
questions.question: What is the primary advantage of a Binary Search Tree over a simple unsorted list?

questions.correct_answer: The algorithm's execution time grows quadratically with the input size.
questions.explanation: Big-O notation describes the upper bound of an algorithm's time or space complexity. O(n^2) means the execution time increases with the square of the input size, indicating a significant performance degradation for large inputs.
options: The algorithm will always perform a fixed number of operations regardless of input size.
The algorithm's execution time grows quadratically with the input size.
The algorithm's execution time grows linearly with the input size.
The algorithm's execution time decreases as the input size grows.
